title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: Ligands with two environmentally switchable excited states, or with separate π/hydrogen-bond and metal-emission channels, can couple sensing with a second function such as proton conduction, gas separation, or electrocatalysis in one rare-earth framework.
explanation: Humidity toggles the enol and keto excited states of HPIF-3COOH and thus energy transfer to Eu(III) for multimodal readout. A Ce-MOF electronically coupled to carboxylated carbon nanotubes lowers charge-transfer resistance and serves both uric-acid sensing and the oxygen-evolution reaction. Thienothiophene–carboxylate Eu-MOFs use π electrons and hydrogen-bond networks for sensing plus proton conduction. A hybrid-ligand microporous Tb-MOF selectively adsorbs C2H2 over CO2 through hydrogen bonds and C–H···π contacts while also acting as a fluorescent probe.
scope: Multifunctional Eu-, Tb-, and Ce-based MOFs and flexible MOF–carbon electrodes.
conditions: Humidity for ESIPT switching; CNT–Ce-MOF electronic coupling in a PVA electrode; microporous hybrid-ligand pores for C2H2/CO2.
caveats: The review later warns that optical, electronic, and magnetic functions in integrated systems can compete, so dual function does not imply synergistic optimization.
